Items in _open_questions are NOT stated in any document we hold and must be confirmed before go-live. Apply: DOCEX_ORG=eva DOCEX_DB=./eva.db python3 org_config.py apply profiles/eva.json
name: Education as a Vaccine
_departments_note: EVA's finance hierarchy: ED/Board → Admin/Finance Team Lead (TLFA) → Finance Coordinator → Finance Officer. The Compliance Officer sits inside Finance but reports to ED/Board for independence, and reviews EVERY payment. TLFA processes the payment on the bank platform; the ED gives final authorisation afterwards — which is why 'tlfa' and 'ed' are separate steps.

departments.name: Program / Admin
departments.description: Initiates requests and assembles supporting documentation

departments.name: Compliance
departments.description: Independent review: deductions captured, approvals obtained, documents complete, donor rules met. Reports to ED/Board.

departments.name: Finance
departments.description: Completeness, accuracy, and budget availability by project and cost centre

departments.name: Admin/Finance Team Lead
departments.description: Raises the payment voucher and processes payment on the bank platform

departments.name: Executive Director
departments.description: Approves all procurements of N300,000 or more

departments.name: Board (Chair + Finance Committee)
departments.description: Approves procurements of N10,000,000 or more — Board Chair plus at least one member of the Finance Committee

workflow._todo: Thresholds below are CONFIRMED from the signed Procurement Policy (see _sources). Still unconfirmed: advance limits and retirement windows, petty cash ceiling, statutory rates — see _open_questions.
workflow._flow: Their process map: Program initiates → Compliance review → Finance review → voucher raised → approval per DOA → TLFA processes payment → ED final authorisation → recorded under project + expense codes → filed for audit.

_grants_note: EVA is a prime/pass-through managing sub-recipients, notably USG-funded. Populate from their signed agreements — donor, project code, value, and the agreement period that drives grant-period blocking.
_features_note: Flags for the EVA-specific engines. All false until the engine behind each one exists and is tested — a flag that turns on nothing is worse than no flag. See EVA_BUILD_PLAN.md for the engine specs (E1–E9).
_modules_note: Top-level product areas this client bought. The nav shows only these. Finance-workflow-only clients don't need the screening or knowledge modules.
_open_questions: DISCREPANCY IN THEIR OWN DOCUMENT: the Procurement Policy reads '300,000 Naira (two hundred thousand Naira)' — the figure and the words disagree. Every other mention says N300,000, so we configured 300,000, but EVA must confirm and correct their policy text.

ADVANCE RETIREMENT WINDOW — not stated in POL-FIN-300.01 (Activity Advances) or 300.04 (Travel Advance). No number appears anywhere in either document. This is a genuine gap in their policy, not a gap in our reading. Ask what the practice is and whether they want it enforced.
ADVANCE LIMITS — no maximum advance amount stated in any of POL-FIN-300.01 to .04.

PETTY CASH CEILING — POL-FIN-100.02 mentions N40,000, but only inside a worked illustration ('It is assumed that EVA/FCT establishes a Petty Cash Fund...'). That is an example, not a policy limit. Confirm the real ceiling per office.

REFINANCING SIGN CONVENTION — blocks payroll (E4). Working interpretation: cost recovery / recharge, salary charged back to a donor grant, shown negative because it offsets the expense line. MUST be confirmed before any payroll code is written.
STATUTORY RATES — PAYE bands, pension rate, WHT rates by payment type, VAT treatment. Not in the documents we hold.
GRANT CODES + AGREEMENT PERIODS — needed for grant-period blocking. Populate from their signed agreements.
MULTI-OFFICE — are HQ / State / field offices a reporting dimension on every transaction, or separate instances?
QUICKBOOKS EXPORT — which format, and does it import as a journal or as bills?

_sources.procurement_three_quotes: EVA Approved Procurement Policy — 'three quotes for procurements estimated to be 300,000 Naira or more'
_sources.approval_below_300k: Procurement Policy, Thresholds and Approval — 'Approvals for procurements below N300,000 can be given by departmental heads or their delegates (who should not be below the grade level of a coordinator)'
_sources.approval_300k_plus: Procurement Policy — 'All procurements involving N300,000 or more ... must be approved by the executive director'
_sources.approval_10m_plus: Procurement Policy — 'Procurements involving N10,000,000 or more ... must be approved by the board chair and at least a member of the finance committee of the board'
_sources.single_source_waiver: Procurement Policy — 'A written justification (procurement waiver) should be provided for single source procurement of value of 200,000 Naira'
